jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Position:**

Program Coordinator

**Department:**

Clinical

**Supervisor:**

Clinical Site Director

**FLSA Status:**

Full-Time; Non-Exempt

**Age of Patient Population Served:**

Adults and Adolescent

**Primary Purpose:**

The Program Coordinator provides comprehensive administrative support to the Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) and Partial Hospitalization Program (PHP) teams while demonstrating a professional and respectful rapport with patients, families, and staff. This Coordinator also provides direct supportive care to selected patients, families, and the clinical team to ensure that services are delivered efficiently and effectively. This position is also the in-person administrative support for on-site outpatient patients and clinicians.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* High School Diploma
* Ability and interest in learning clinical information and criteria. Knowledge of medical terminology
* Computer literacy and communication skills.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Associate's or Bachelor's degree in social work or similar concentration.
* 1–2 years of experience in a healthcare setting is a plus.
* Google Workspace & EMR experience.
* Medical Assistant certification is a plus.

**Core Competencies:**

* Independent Judgment & Problem-Solving
* Organization & Time Management
* Professionalism, Integrity & Reliability
* Communication & Interpersonal Skills
* Adaptability & Team Collaboration
* Emotional Resilience & Patient Awareness

**Essential Functions:**

* Provide administrative support to the Program teams, including the Program Manager/Clinical Operations Director, Clinicians, and patients.
* Demonstrate professional and respectful rapport when interacting with all stakeholders, including patients, family members, co-workers, vendors, and other clinical staff.
* Conducts administrative duties including but not limited to:

  + Coordinate with Admissions to welcome new families to the program.
  + Maintain patient tracking list, updating as needed.
  + Scheduling group and session appointments for IOP/PHP patients.
  + Generating video calls for virtual IOP/PHP appointments.
  + Checking in and checking out patients.
  + Uploading registration paperwork.
  + Responding to email inquiries in a thorough, timely, and courteous manner.
  + Collecting and uploading paperwork.
  + Responding to the needs of patients, clinicians and program managers.
* Work closely with the Clinical Operations Director/Program Manager to coordinate group coverage as needed and provide updates about patient attendance and census.
* Report and track patient attendance and appointment charges daily.
* Facilitate the completion of daily electronic questionnaires with IOP/PHP patients.
* Attend weekly IOP/PHP treatment team meetings to review enrollment of new patients, identify scheduling and discharge planning needs, and facilitate next steps with scheduling.
* Taking vitals (weight, height, blood pressure) and drug test samples as needed.
* Clerical duties include copying, mailing, faxing, scanning, and sorting documentation.
* Performing other miscellaneous job-related duties as assigned.
* Submitting purchase orders for PHP/IOP Programs and the office as needed.
* Support Clinical Operations Director/Program Manager with Discharge coordination and administrative needs.
* Learn and perform general front desk duties to support outpatient administrative coverage.

  + Answering the phone, providing information, and routing calls appropriately.
  + Greeting outpatients and connecting them with their clinicians.
  + General facility maintenance and upkeep.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Mobility: Ability to move around the treatment facility as needed, including walking, standing, and occasional lifting or moving objects.

**Work Environment:**

* The work environment is conducted in an office setting.

**Travel Requirements:**

* Must be able to work in person at the Berkeley Clinic.

**BACA’s Core Values:**

BACA employees form a team with the highest standards who are individually and collectively committed to provide the highest level of care and service for our patient, their families and referents. As such, we require all of our employees to embody our core values detailed below:

**Integrity**: We are honest and accountable for our performance. We treat our patients and colleagues with respect and dignity.

**Quality:** We focus on consistent and competent performance of our duties. Careful attention to communication and follow-through produces excellent delivery of care.

**Compassion:** BACA prides itself on being a safe, comfortable, and contained environment that supports healing, recovery and hope. Every patient is treated with empathy, caring, and kindness.

**Collaboration:** We employ a “whole person” perspective to treatment. To that end, our program not only focuses on the patient, but the family system as well. We pool resources from patients, families, peers, partners and professionals to deliver exceptional care.

**Service:** We aid by creating a safe, calm shelter for our patients to risk exploring emotional issues that emerge in treatment.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Housing Place-Based Services
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Homebridge serves a high risk, high needs, complex-diagnosed population with a combination of domestic, personal, and paramedical homecare functions funded through IHSS. Our work allows an often-underserved population to live safely in their community. Homebridge offers a dynamic, fast-paced work environment with 350+ unionized field workers and 90+ internal office staff.

POSITION SUMMARY

Homebridge is seeking an experienced and mission-driven Program Manager to lead our MOHCD-funded Housing Place-Based Services program (Program Area 2). This role designs and oversees the quality of Homebridge's resident skills-building workshop model at four San Francisco properties, leads a team of trainers who are the primary deliverers of workshop content, facilitates selected sessions, manages day-to-day program coordination, and serves as Homebridge's primary liaison to MOHCD and to property management and lead service provider partners across all sites. The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management skills with experience navigating government grant compliance and building trust-based partnerships with affordable housing operators and service providers.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Program Design & Oversight

* Lead delivery at Windsor, Pacific Bay Inn, Minna Lee (DISH), and 1100 Ocean Avenue (Mercy Housing): four workshop series per property per year, 4–6 sessions each.
* Design and continuously refine the workshop curriculum framework across MOHCD's eligible content areas: Health & Wellness, Economic Mobility, Education, Life Skills, and Money Management.
* Ensure all programming is trauma-informed, culturally responsive, accessible, and additive to — not duplicative of — each site's existing on-site lead service provider programming.
* Establish and monitor performance targets aligned with MOHCD's Required Work Plan Table.

Trainer Team Leadership

* Lead, onboard, and coach a team of trainers who are the primary deliverers of workshop content.
* Assign trainers by site, topic, language, and schedule, and manage coverage.
* Provide ongoing training and support on trauma-informed practice, de-escalation, and culturally responsive facilitation.

Workshop Delivery & Program Coordination

* Facilitate selected workshop sessions directly, and cover sessions when needed.
* Manage day-to-day program coordination, including series calendars, room reservations, building logistics, and resident outreach and sign-ups with partner staff.
* Track attendance and outreach records, and manage incentives, refreshments, tablets, and workshop materials.

Partner & MOHCD Relations

* Serve as Homebridge's primary point of contact with MOHCD for this grant, including reporting, compliance, and site visits.
* Maintain relationships with property management and on-site lead service provider partners across all sites, including at least weekly coordination once services are operational.
* Lead partnership development for new sites, including securing Letters of Intent and Letters of Support.

Data, Evaluation & Compliance

* Oversee data collection, outcome tracking, and the annual client satisfaction survey process across all sites.
* Prepare and submit required MOHCD reports and deliverables.
* Ensure grant compliance with MOHCD requirements, including budget adherence and eligible use of funds.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

* Bachelor's degree in social work, public administration, public health, or a related field required; Master's degree preferred.
* 3+ years of experience in program management, ideally within affordable housing, homeless services, or community-based nonprofit settings.
* 2+ years of supervisory or team-lead experience, plus experience delivering adult workshops or training.
* Demonstrated experience managing government grants, including reporting, compliance, and budget oversight.
* Strong understanding of trauma-informed, culturally responsive service models.
* Excellent relationship-management skills with property managers, service provider partners, and government funders.
* Strong written communication skills, including grant reporting and narrative writing.
* Bilingual English/Spanish a plus.

Required Training and Certifications

* Trauma-informed care training completion required within first 90 days of hire (provided by Homebridge, or prior certification accepted).
* Mandated reporter training completion required.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

* Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Public Administration, Public Health, Human Services, Community Development, or a related field required;
  + Master's degree preferred.
* Minimum of 3–5 years of program management experience, preferably in affordable housing, homeless services, community-based organizations, or nonprofit settings.
* Minimum of 2 years of supervisory or team leadership experience, including staff development, coaching, and performance management.
* Demonstrated experience managing government-funded grants or contracts, including budget oversight, compliance, reporting, and deliverable management.
* Experience developing and facilitating community-based workshops or educational programming, building community partnerships, and working with diverse populations using trauma-informed and culturally responsive approaches.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is hybrid, combining office-based program management and MOHCD reporting work with regular travel across San Francisco partner properties for site visits and partner meetings. Some evening or weekend availability may be required for community events.

Our mission is to create and support programs that protect the health and autonomy of vulnerable individuals and promote equity and social justice to improve the well-being of our entire community. Compassionate care for vulnerable populations.

**Workplace Culture:**

Cardea is dedicated to creating a workplace that celebrates diversity and actively seeks to include underrepresented communities. We believe that diversity drives innovation and fosters a more dynamic, inclusive, and productive work environment. We value unique perspectives, experiences, and talents, and we are committed to providing equitable opportunities for growth and advancement. Join us in building a team that reflects the rich diversity of our society and let's make a positive impact together.

Our Cardea CARE(S) Values include:

* Compassion
    
  Big heart, steady presence
* Accountability
    
  We own it: the work, the follow-through, the impact.
* Respect

We offer access to competitive and comprehensive healthcare benefits such as: Medical, dental, vision, EAP, life insurance, long-term disability, HSA or FSA, Dependent Care FSA, voluntary benefits, paid sick leave, paid vacation time, birthday time off, and 401(k) with up to 3.5% employer match.

jobs.title: Patient Navigator
jobs.description:
**Trial Library is an AI-native research platform with a mission to improve healthcare outcomes by expanding access to precision medicine.**

**About Trial Library**

Trial Library is an AI-native enrollment and care navigation platform that accelerates access to precision medicine. In collaboration with biopharmaceutical manufacturers, payers, and health systems, Trial Library enables the delivery of clinical trials as a standard care option - improving patient access, advancing oncology outcomes, and reducing the total cost of care. Backed by leading healthcare venture capital firms, Trial Library’s platform is currently deployed in 840+ clinics and 3,000+ providers nationwide.

### **About the Role:**

As a Patient Navigator, you'll do more than guide patients through the clinical trial enrollment process—you'll help shape the future of how patients access precision medicine.

You will serve as a trusted partner to patients with cancer and their caregivers, helping them understand clinical trial opportunities, overcome barriers to care, and navigate complex healthcare systems with empathy and confidence. You'll also work cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Clinical teams to continuously improve the patient experience and influence how our navigation services evolve.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone with a nursing background who combines clinical expertise with a passion for patient advocacy and enjoys building new processes in a fast-paced, mission-driven startup environment.

### **Your Responsibilities**

**Patient Navigation & Advocacy**

* Serve as a trusted liaison between patients, caregivers, healthcare providers, and clinical research sites.
* Guide patients through the clinical trial referral, screening, and enrollment journey.
* Educate patients and families on clinical trial opportunities and precision medicine.
* Identify and help remove barriers to care by connecting patients with appropriate resources.
* Coordinate medical record collection and facilitate seamless handoffs to research sites.
* Maintain ongoing communication and support throughout the patient journey.

**Cross-Functional Partnership**

* Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Clinical teams to improve the patient experience.
* Respond to inquiries from patients, providers, and internal stakeholders.
* Provide feedback that informs new workflows, features, and service offerings.

**Operations**

* Document patient interactions and maintain accurate case records.
* Contribute to SOPs, educational content, and operational documentation.
* Track key navigation metrics and prepare reports on patient outcomes and team activities.
* Help build and scale Trial Library's patient navigation program as the company grows.

### **Your Qualifications**

* Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN), Associate Degree in Nursing (ADN), or equivalent nursing degree required. *An active RN or LPN license is not required.*
* 2+ years of experience supporting oncology patients, patient navigation, clinical research, or a related healthcare setting.
* Working knowledge of clinical trials and the patient enrollment process.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to explain complex medical information to diverse audiences.
* Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple patients, priorities, and deadlines.
* Demonstrated empathy, sound judgment, and a patient-first approach.
* Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with evolving priorities.
* Proficiency with electronic health records (EHRs), CRM systems, or similar healthcare technology platforms.
* Experience working at an early-stage or high-growth startup.

### **Nice to Have**

* Oncology clinical trial enrollment or study coordination experience.
* Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC), CCRP, or other clinical research certification.
* Experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, or Operations teams to improve workflows or services.
* Experience developing SOPs, patient education materials, or operational processes.
* Multilingual (Spanish, Mandarin, Cantonese, or other languages commonly spoken by oncology patient populations).
* Familiarity with precision medicine, biomarker testing, or molecular diagnostics.

This is a hybrid role based in San Francisco, CA, with a requirement of three days per week in the office; Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. The salary range for this position is **$68,000–$102,000** per year and reflects a good faith estimate of base pay for candidates working in this location. Final compensation will be based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

### **Why Trial Library**

* Meaningful impact — helping patients access clinical trials faster through better technology and workflows
* High ownership environment — autonomy to build, test, and influence strategy across the business
* Collaborative team culture — low ego, high trust, and close partnership across functions
* Opportunity for growth — join at an early stage with meaningful exposure to company-building and decision-making

### **Our Core Values**

* Ally is our favorite moniker
* The broadest reach is worth the effort
* Celebrate measurable improvements in access and outcomes
* Fearless advocates for representation in research
* Incentives matter to stakeholders choosing our products
* Taking initiative is actually giving
* We are accountable for the experience of patients and providers
* Empathy and humility are the real dynamic duo

### **Our Benefits & Perks**

* Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and eligible dependents, along with disability, life, and supplemental insurance options designed to support your overall well-being.
* Time Off & Workplace Support: Flexible paid time off, observed company holidays, and a one-time home office stipend to help you create a productive and comfortable remote workspace w

**About the role**  
  
The People Partner team provides HR support to Uber's leaders, managers, and employees, especially in the moments that matter. The team helps drive engagement, strengthen the employee experience, and support Uber's growth through regional and global People initiatives.  
  
We’re looking for an experienced People Partner to support employees across our Tech organizations.This person will act as a trusted advisor to managers and employees on people matters including performance, engagement, employee relations, organizational health, and broader People priorities.  
  
The ideal candidate is data-driven, organized, adaptable, and passionate about improving processes and the employee experience in a fast-paced environment.  
  
**What you'll do**

* Act as a HR advisor, mentor, and partner to employees, managers, and leaders, and manage risk mitigation and de-escalating/resolving HR matters.
* Provide HR guidance, managing clients, business, and company needs against risks, to solve HR problems, build relationships, and increase manager, and leader capability..
* Use data and insights to identify trends, inform decisions, and drive continuous improvement in HR delivery.

For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $131,000 per year - USD $145,000 per year.

For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you.  
  
You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.  
  
Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.title: Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
**The Problem**

Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.

What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.

We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

**Who We Are**

Amae Health is a Series B, venture-backed Public Benefit Corporation delivering specialty outpatient care for people with severe mental illness through high-acuity, in-person clinics nationwide.

Our integrated model brings psychiatry, therapy, primary care, dietitians, and community support together under one roof. Leading health systems—including **NewYork-Presbyterian, Cedars-Sinai, Mass General Brigham, Novant Health, and CommonSpirit**—partner with us to expand this level of care.

Alongside care delivery, we are building the science and technology the field has long lacked—proprietary clinical protocols, novel measurement, and an AI-driven data platform designed for severe mental illness.

The impact: fewer hospitalizations, greater stability, and more people living meaningful lives in their communities.

**The Team**

We are clinicians, operators, technologists, and scientists who chose Amae because the problem is hard and the stakes are real. We are not interested in incremental improvements to a broken system—we are redefining it.

Our teams work cross-functionally because the work demands it. The psychiatrist informs the product roadmap. Engineers understand the clinical complexity their technology must solve. Researchers sit alongside the operators running the clinics their work measures.

Every function—finance, product, people, growth, technology—exists to serve one goal: better outcomes for the people we care for.

**The Role**

The **Strategy & Operations** team at Amae plays a critical role in driving the programs and systems that support delivery of excellent care. This highly cross-functional role will work across a diverse range of teams and functions, leveraging complex problem-solving skills in a growth-oriented organization. This role is located in San Francisco, in office 5 days a week.

**What You Will Work On**

* Own the creation, rollout, and ongoing refinement of projects that support day-to-day behavioral health delivery; build structured workflows, playbooks, and feedback loops
* Partner with clinical and operational leaders to identify bottlenecks and design solutions that scale across markets
* Use data, user feedback, and operational insights to evaluate program performance and identify improvement opportunities
* Drive alignment across clinical, operations, product, and leadership teams to ensure programs are implemented smoothly and sustainably
* Lead communication, training, and rollout plans for new initiatives

**What You'll Have**

* 3+ years of experience within private equity management consulting, investment banking, venture capital, or within a healthcare organization driving initiatives from ideation to implementation
* Scrappy, self-starter mindset who vigorously looks for ways to grow an early-stage company
* Proven experience structuring and leading projects to drive successful outcomes
* Strong analytical, financial modeling, and problem-solving skills with high proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Experience in a startup and/or entrepreneurial environment; ability to thrive in a fast-paced culture, growing 0–1
* Passion and interest for the mental health space
* Bachelor's Degree required

**What We're Building**

Most healthcare companies ask you to optimize an existing system. We're building one that has never existed.

* A national care model designed for the highest-acuity patients in behavioral health.
* Precision medicine for severe mental illness, using multimodal clinical, behavioral, and social data to personalize treatment.
* A clinical operating system that integrates longitudinal data, real-time patient signals, and purpose-built tools into a single decision layer.
* New science and measurement frameworks to define what real outcomes look like in SMI.
* A health-system partnership model proving coordinated SMI care can work at scale.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Amae Health is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. **Base salary range for this role is $125,000 to $165,000 per year** based on a full-time schedule; the compensation package will include equity. Total compensation includes comprehensive medical/dental/vision, unlimited PTO, parental leave, and programs built around employee well-being. We'll share specifics during the interview process.

*Amae Health is building the care platform, the precision medicine, and the frontier science that severe mental illness has never had. If you want to be part of creating something this hard and this important, something that has never been done, we'd like to talk.*

**What We Value**

* **We center care in all we do.** Empathy is not a brand value. It's how we make clinical decisions, build products, and treat each other.
* **We challenge convention.** The existing system is the problem. We question it, we test alternatives, and we move with urgency when something works.
* **We take the work seriously, not ourselves.** High standards and humanity are not in tension. We hold a hard bar for quality while leaving room for humor and levity.
* **Your job isn't done until the job is done.** We close gaps, we follow through, and we don't hide behind titles or org charts.
* **We win together and fail toge

jobs.title: Certification Operations and Policy Program Manager
jobs.description:
Technical Success - San Francisco

**About the Team**

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

**About the Role**

As Certification Operations and Policy Program Manager, you will build and run the processes that make OpenAI certifications accessible, fair, and reliable for candidates and the organizations that rely on them.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role on the Certification team, with no direct reports. You will define candidate policies, turn them into practical processes, and own their implementation as the program grows. This is not a general program-management or support-only role: it combines policy development with hands-on operational delivery.

You will work closely with the Certification team, product and technical teams, Legal, Privacy, Security, Accessibility, Support, and delivery vendors to define operational standards and apply policies consistently and fairly. You will connect the partners needed to turn certification requirements into workable candidate processes.

You will start with early certification launches and build reusable playbooks, service standards, and review processes for live and virtual delivery. Initially, you will also triage escalated vendor and candidate cases, resolve routine delivery or credential-access issues, and route substantive appeals through the established independent-review process.

Success means candidates know what to expect, delivery partners know what to do when something goes wrong, and sensitive decisions are documented and independently reviewed.

**In this role, you will:**

* Define candidate-facing policies and communications across the certification journey, including eligibility, registration, exam rules, retakes, exceptions, expiration, and renewal. Partner with the Certification team to translate program requirements into policy and with Legal, product, technical teams, and vendors to build the processes that uphold it.
* Own the accommodations process from request through delivery. Work with Accessibilityation throughout.
* Own certification records and evidence workflows teams.
* Own vendor workflows and operational delivery standards, including handoffs, service levels, readiness checks, and escalation paths. Initially serve as the first point of contact for escalated delivery and credential-access cases, coordinating vendor fixes, candidate communications, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate the response to exam integrity incidents, including suspected cheating, impersonation, or unauthorized sharing of exam content. Work with Security, Legal, and delivery vendors to document evidence, route cases to the appropriate decision-makers, and communicate and implement approved outcomes, such as score invalidation or credential revocation.
* Administer appeals and independent reviews. Set intake and response timelines, assemble the case record, screen for conflicts of interest, and route decisions to qualified reviewers who were not involved in the original decision. Document and communicate outcomes without deciding cases you administer.
* Coordinate Legal guidance on candidate policiesance to improve delivery.

**You might thrive in this role if you:**

* Have owned operations or candidate policy for professional certification, licensure, high-stakes assessment, or a similarly governed program.
* Have taken a certification, licensure, or comparable high-stakes program from launch readiness through live delivery, and can show how you used operational data and candidate feedback to identify recurring problems and improve delivery.
* Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.
* Have defined candidate-facing policies and translated them into clear communications and operational workflows that internal teams and vendors can apply consistently.
* Have built or run an accommodations processation.
* Have administered incidents, complaints, appeals, or exceptions, documenting decisions and maintaining review by people who were not involved in the original decision.
* Have managed external delivery vendors against service standards and followed through when those standards were not met.
* Have handled sensitive candidate, assessment, or credential records and worked with privacy or security teams on appropriate controls.
* Have translated complex policies into candidate communications and operational guidance, and coordinated implementation across vendors and internal teams without direct reporting authority.
* Have personally written operational playbooks, checked launch readiness, triaged cases, and improved delivery processes.
* Have resolved time-sensitive operational issues within established policy and escalated exceptions to the appropriate decision-makers.
* Have applied accessibility, fairness, and credential-integrity policies consistently in candidate-facing operations.

* Launching or scaling technical certifications acr

**HOW MIGHT YOU DEFY IMAGINATION?**

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will be responsible for representing TEPEZZA to physicians and health care professionals, establishing product sales, and performing total territory account management.

The Specialty Account Manager is responsible for providing account management support to accounts within a specific geography in the designated marketplace with a focus on issues specific to their designated accounts. We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The Specialty Account Manager we seek is a motivated professional with these qualifications.

Bachelor's Degree and 3 years of sales experience within pharmaceutical, biotech or medical device industry or hospital sales experience

jobs.title: Care Coordinator: Timmy's Home
jobs.description:
**About Cardea Health:**

Cardea Health is a non-profit organization dedicated to providing compassionate health care to marginalized populations.

**Misson Statement:**

Our mission is to create and support programs that protect the health and autonomy of vulnerable individuals and promote equity and social justice to improve the well-being of our entire community. Compassionate care for vulnerable populations.

**Workplace Culture:**

Cardea is dedicated to creating a workplace that celebrates diversity and actively seeks to include underrepresented communities. We believe that diversity drives innovation and fosters a more dynamic, inclusive, and productive work environment. We value unique perspectives, experiences, and talents, and we are committed to providing equitable opportunities for growth and advancement. Join us in building a team that reflects the rich diversity of our society and let's make a positive impact together.

Our Cardea CARE(S) Values include:

* Compassion
    
  Big heart, steady presence
* Accountability
    
  We own it: the work, the follow-through, the impact.
* Respect
    
  We assume good intent and keep it real
* Engagement
    
  We lean in and figure it out together.
* Support
    
  We’ve got each other across roles, teams, and sites.

These values guide how we care for residents, collaborate with colleagues, and represent Cardea Health in the community.

**Primary Work Location:** Timmy's Home

This position is based primarily at Timmy's Home, a Cardea Health interim housing program serving individuals experiencing homelessness who may have complex medical, behavioral health, and social service needs.

Employees working at this location support residents in a housing-focused environment centered on stabilization, health, dignity, and connection to community resources and permanent housing opportunities.

Depending on the position, employees may regularly interact with residents, healthcare providers, case managers, housing navigators, community partners, visitors, and government agencies.

**Job Summary:**

The care coordinator will assist clinical staff and residents in the coordination of medical and behavioral health care.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Maintain a calendar of upcoming resident medical and behavioral health appointments. Communicate upcoming appointments to clients, clinical staff, and transportation services
* Assist clinical staff and site-based residents in the scheduling of client medical and behavioral health appointments.
    
  Communicate with local pharmacies regarding site-based resident prescriptions. At the direction of nursing staff request medication refills, deliveries, and transfers
* Request relevant medical records of site-based residents from hospitals and community clinics. Transmit medical records and other authorized requested documentation to partner clinics to facilitate care coordination
* Interface with site-based resident healthcare coverage plans to avoid interruption in services and facilitate care
* Take telephone messages and provide feedback and answers to patient/physician/pharmacy calls
* Ensure adherence to infection control standards on site among staff and residents
* Answer calls to the nursing station and respond independently to when appropriate
* Assist nursing staff with light clerical duties including filing and making copies
* Maintain confidentiality in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
* Practice harm reduction principles on site, including interventions that minimize harmful effects of substance use while treating all residents with dignity and respect
* Other duties as assigned
* Constant work around and/or with people OR Interaction with patients, clients, and external customers
* Clinical setting in a permanent supportive housing site

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* High School Diploma or equivalent
* Must be authorized to live and work in the U.S
* Must be at least 18 years of age
* Must have personal, reliable transportation to and from work sites and shifts

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Prior experience with homeless or incarcerated populations is desirable
* Self-directed and able to work with minimal supervision
* Detailed oriented and highly organized
* Must provide proof of COVID vaccination or willing to be vaccinated
* Prior experience with homeless or incarcerated populations is highly desirable
* Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel

**Physical Requirements:**

This position requires a combination of desk-based and active work activities.

Essential physical activities may include:

* Frequent sitting, standing, and walking.
* Movement throughout program sites, office locations, or community settings.
* Occasional stair climbing.
* Reaching, bending, kneeling, and crouching.
* Transporting supplies, equipment, files, or materials.
* Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull up to 25 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Work Environment:**

Cardea Health program locations operate within supportive housing, interim housing, medical respite, and community-based environments serving individuals experiencing homelessness and other vulnerable populations.

**Benefit:**

We offer access to competitive and comprehensive healthcare benefits such as: Medical, dental, vision, EAP, life insurance, long-term disability, HSA or FSA, Dependent Care FSA, voluntary benefits, paid sick leave, paid vacation time, birthday time off, and 401(k) with up to 3.5% employer match.

Benefit eligibility varies based on employment status, scheduled hours, and plan requirements. Full-time employees are generally eligible for employer-sponsored benefit contributions. Eligible part-time employees may participate in available benefit programs subject to plan terms. Per diem employees are generally not eligible for employer-sponsored benefits except as required by applicable federal, state, or local law or as otherwi

jobs.title: Client Services Enrollment Specialist
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

BANANAS Inc. is seeking a **Client Services Enrollment Counselor.** The Client Services Enrollment Counselor is responsible for contacting and enrolling new families from the BANANAS Eligibility List (BEL) into our California Alternative Payment Programs (CAPP). This position also transfers eligible families into our CalWORKs Stage 2 program while providing excellent customer service throughout the enrollment process.

This position performs duties in support of BANANAS’ mission and program operations. The duties listed below represent the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals to perform these essential functions.

Job duties, responsibilities, work locations, and schedules may change based on organizational needs.

**About BANANAS Inc.**

BANANAS is a nonprofit organization that supports families, children, and early care and education providers. Our programs help families connect with all types of child care options, from family child care, home-based settings, preschool centers, family, friend, neighbor caregivers, and nannies, so they can work or continue their education. Providers are supported with technical assistance and professional development. We are experts in the field of early care and education, and our wide variety of services supports families and child care providers in raising early learners. We offer workshops, playgroups, coaching, and support groups for parents and caregivers. Low-income families are supported with financial assistance so they can access quality child care. BANANAS is a great place to work with colleagues who care about their clients, our youngest learners, and each other.

**Primary Duties and Responsibilities**

* Contact families from the BANANAS Eligibility List (BEL).
* Meet with parents/guardians and/or child care providers to verify initial assessment information.
* Complete family applications, obtain signatures on childcare provider agreements, and enter families' and child care providers' information into KinderSystems database.
* Calculate income to determine family eligibility.
* Enter information for upcoming documentation requests and changes into the KinderSystem database.
* Clarify and answer questions to ensure parents and providers understand the program policies and procedures.
* Maintain a thorough understanding of all guidelines, regulations, and policies and procedures.
* Send Notice Of Action (NOA) and Contract Amendments to parents and child care providers, as needed.
* Receive and enroll CalWORKs Stage 2 transfers from Stage 1 agencies.
* Enroll eligible Stage 2 families who come to BANANAS within our service areas.
* Communicate with and enroll any out-of-county transfers (CalWORKs) from other agencies.
* Submit family files to Quality Assurance (QA) for review
* Conduct child care provider intakes and enter information into KinderSystems database
* Maintain a small caseload
* Monitor caseloads to determine families' needs for child care services
* Recertify families and update information in files and KinderSystems database

**Secondary Duties and Responsibilities**

* Assist with client calls, walk-ins, and inquiries while collecting and documenting information in client files or the KinderSystems database, as required.
* Maintain a working knowledge of Resource & Referral services.
* Coordinate one annual staff development training for the Client Services team.
* Perform all duties in accordance with organizational policies, values, and strategic priorities. Assume additional responsibilities and complete special projects as assigned.

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of duties. Responsibilities may change at any time, with or without notice.

**Role Scope**

This position is responsible for performing assigned duties in support of BANANAS’ programs and operations. This role does not include supervisory responsibility over staff.

Employees are expected to follow established procedures, collaborate with team members, and escalate issues as appropriate.

**Work Location Flexibility and Travel Requirements**

This position may be assigned to work at different locations to support program needs, coverage requirements, and operational priorities. Employees are expected to demonstrate flexibility in work assignments and locations.

Travel between BANANAS’ locations during the workday will be considered compensable hours worked for non-exempt staff, and business mileage and approved work-related expenses will be reimbursed in accordance with California Labor Code Section 2802 and BANANAS’ policy.

This position is assigned to a designated, fully equipped BANANAS workspace. While partial telecommuting may be permitted as a convenience to the employee, on-site workspace and resources remain fully available. Voluntary remote work expenses associated with a home office (such as home internet or utilities) are not deemed necessary job expenditures and are not subject to reimbursement, unless otherwise required by law or pre-approved in writing by the Human Resources Department. Employees are expected to utilize BANANAS-provided communication tools and equipment for all business tasks; use of personal devices for work purposes must be pre-authorized.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Required Qualifications**

* High School Diploma or Equivalent
* 1-2 years of data entry experience
* 2 or more years of customer service experience
* Basic math skills
* Excellent oral and written communication skills
* Computer experience: Microsoft Word, Excel and Google Suite

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Knowledge of KinderSystem and NetSuite, or similar systems
* Knowledge of California child care laws and regulations
* Social services background
* Understanding of State regulations

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to communicate and exchange informati

jobs.title: Case Manager - HIV
jobs.description:
SUMMARY:

The Case Manager will provide comprehensive individualized case management services to people living with HIV (PLWH) in Alameda County. It is the responsibility of the HIV Case Manager to provide: a wide spectrum of services as a part of a primary care team; help to improve the health and well-being of our primary care patients and promote team functioning; and provide clinically and culturally sensitive outreach services to marginally housed adults in order to engage them in primary care services. Interventions may include crisis intervention, brief behavioral interventions, psychosocial assessments, collaboration with outside service providers, and appropriate internal/external referrals. Strong attention to detail as well as above-average interpersonal and organizational skills are necessary for the position. The position will require travel to sites throughout Alameda County.

This position reports to the HIV Program Manager.

This position is represented by SEIU-UHW. Salaries and benefits are set by a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), and an employee in this position must remain a member in good standing of SEIU-UHW, as defined in the CBA.

JOB DUTIES:

* Care coordination
* Primary Care coordination
* Help retain PLWH in care at the East Oakland Health Center. This includes reengaging patients who have had a lapse in medical care.
* Coordinates health care for individuals in need of assistance with adherence to medication. The goal is to help all PLWH to maintain an undetectable viral load. Assists with medication reconciliation.
* Links newly identified PLWH to available social services, including legal, housing, transportation, mental health, substance abuse, and pain management services.
* Tracks client follow up and care plan outcomes. Coordinates with medical providers regarding need for enhanced services.
* Documents client progress, referrals, encounters, services, and treatment progress in the centralized client management system to allow appropriate sharing with others program service providers.
* Assists with patients navigating barriers to care, treatment and social support:
* Assists patients in navigating the requirements of medical insurance.
* Enrolls patients in AIDS Drug Assistance Program.
* Eligibility determination to ensure access to community services.
* Tracks, manages, and facilitates specialty referrals to ensure patients are successfully linked to services.
* Makes appointments and completes reminder calls for primary care provider panel.
* Documentation
* Enters all encounters and units of service into the electronic medical record Epic, ARIES, and other data management systems as required.
* Maintains documentation of services to allow compliance with required reporting.
* Maintains strict adherence to all program requirements and deadlines including report deadlines and timely completeness of documentation for site visits and audits.
* Health coaching (patient self-management support)
* Coaches PLWH in self-management (e.g. medication adherence, lifestyle) including self-care skills.
* Assists patients in developing and executing health-related action plans or behavior changes based on client goals.
* Navigates problem-solving with patients as they encounter obstacles to achieving health-related goals.
* Conducts brief interventions with patients regarding alcohol and tobacco use and other behavioral health issues as appropriate.
* Agency and clinic meetings
* Participates in weekly case conferences with the HIV-Access team and monthly HIV Care and Prevention team meetings.
* Represents the HIV Access Program at regular meetings of the Alameda County Office of AIDS and the HIV Access division of the Community Health Consortium Network.
* Coordinates with other clinics within Lifelong Medical Care and across Alameda and Contra Costa Counties.
* Actively participates in clinic team meetings with internal staff and external partners.
* Other tasks
* Coordinate with the LifeLong Street Medicine teams to support PLWH who are homeless connect with the East Oakland Health Center or other LifeLong clinics, enroll in benefits, and connect to other social services.
* Contributes to clinic quality improvement planning and implementation.
* Coordinates operation of special projects as assigned by supervisor.
* Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

* Commitment to the provision of services for the underserved with demonstrated ability and sensitivity in working with a variety of people from low-income populations, with diverse educational, lifestyle, ethnic, and cultural origins.
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills with the ability to handle sensitive issues in a confidential, positive, and professional manner.
* Strong organizational, administrative, multi-tasking, prioritization, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to seek direction/approval on essential matters, yet work independently with little onsite supervision, using professional judgment and diplomacy.
* Work in a team-oriented environment with a number of professionals with different work styles and support needs.
* Conduct oneself in internal and external settings in a way that reflects positively on LifeLong Medical Care as an organization of professional, confident, and sensitive staff.
* Ability to see how one’s work intersects with that of other departments of LifeLong Medical Care and that of other partner organizations.
* Be creative and mature with a “can do,” proactive attitude and an ability to continuously “scan” the environment, identifying and taking advantage of opportunities for improvement.

Job Requirements:

* Prior experience in counseling patients, either in person or by phone.
* Proficient in MS Office/Excel.
* Strong customer service approach to problem solving and conflict resolution.
* Work/volunteer experience with and a commitment to serve people who are living with HIV/AIDS, people experiencing homelessness,

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
The **Program Manager** provides leadership and guidance for one or more programs. This role supervises staff, develops program policy, and performs outreach in coordination with other MNC’s programs.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS / RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Primary Functions**

* Provide 1:1 supervision to staff/and follow-ups with supervisees and documents accordingly.
* Maintain accurate program records and submit data in accordance with funding and reporting requirements, submitting monthly reports to SFGetCare and reports to associate Director on the 5th of each month.
* Advocates for participant needs, providing referral information to internal and external services based on individual participant needs. Provides individual follow-up services to participants as needed and maintains daily records.
* Provides up to date information and clarification regarding programs such as Medicare, Medicaid, CalFresh, formal supportive and social services.
* Provides translation assistance, both verbal and written, to assist clients with specific services.
* Coordinate with other programs and provide support as needed.
* Act as a liaison with school, community, public agencies, and parents/guardians of participants.
* Plan outreach and resource events for the community.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Youth Access Point
jobs.description:
**About us:** 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic is a community-based agency providing youth in the Bayview Hunters Point with medical and behavioral health services that encourage them to make decisions that support their health, safety, and development. 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic also manages a number of successful Transitional Age Youth (TAY) housing stabilization programs and one of the city’s few Youth Access Points.

**Program info:**The Youth Access Point (YAP) Program Manager oversees the operations of 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic's Youth Access Point and SFSU Rapid Rehousing (RRH) programs.

3rd Street operates one of San Francisco's Youth Access Points at our drop-in sites in Bayview and Hunters Point. The Youth Access Point serves as the frontline to San Francisco's Homelessness Response System, where transitional-age youth (ages 18–24) access Coordinated Entry services. These services include Problem Solving, housing assessments, referrals to emergency and long-term housing programs, and connections to supportive services designed to help young people achieve housing stability.

Our work takes place in a dynamic, high-intensity environment where participant needs, staffing demands, program priorities, and external requirements can shift quickly. The YAP Program Manager must be comfortable navigating complexity, responding to urgent situations, managing competing priorities, and leading a team through the realities of frontline service delivery.

The Youth Access Point Program Manager is responsible for the effective delivery, management, and continuous improvement of housing services for young adults. This position provides direct supervision and oversight of YAP and SFSU RRH staff and operations, including service planning and implementation, program and resource development, contract management, and personnel management, including hiring, coaching, training, and performance evaluation.

This is a highly hands-on management position that requires a balance of strategic leadership, program development, and day-to-day operational involvement. The Program Manager must be prepared to move fluidly between managing program operations, supporting staff through complex situations, responding to participant crises, addressing administrative and compliance demands, and ensuring program goals and deliverables are met.

The YAP and housing landscape is continually evolving, with frequent changes in local policies, funding priorities, eligibility requirements, service models, and system-wide expectations. The Program Manager must be comfortable operating in an environment where procedures and priorities may change frequently and where established processes are not always in place. This position will play an active role in developing new programs, building out service offerings, refining existing models, and translating emerging opportunities and requirements into effective program operations. The successful candidate must be comfortable building while simultaneously managing day-to-day operations.

The role requires a high degree of resilience, sound judgment, adaptability, and emotional intelligence. The successful candidate must be able to remain grounded and solution-oriented under pressure, navigate ambiguity, manage competing demands, and maintain accountability even when resources are limited or circumstances are challenging. This person must be willing to roll up their sleeves, step into operational gaps when necessary, and lead by example.

The Program Manager collects and analyzes outcomes data, prepares management reports, and leads significant program initiatives and improvement efforts. In partnership with the Assistant Director of Housing, the Program Manager represents the agency with funders, government agencies, and community providers. The position requires close collaboration with internal and external partners and may include direct service responsibilities such as case management, care coordination, crisis intervention, and mental health rehabilitation services.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

The following is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the Housing Program Manager. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned as needed.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

**Professional Development & Self-Leadership**

* Demonstrates emotional intelligence, self-awareness, and the ability to regulate emotions in high-pressure and emotionally demanding situations.
* Demonstrates resilience and adaptability when navigating organizational changes, staffing challenges, competing priorities, and unexpected operational demands.
* Maintains a solution-oriented approach when faced with challenges, ambiguity, and setbacks; takes initiative rather than waiting for direction.
* Demonstrates the ability to receive feedback, reflect on performance, acknowledge mistakes, and make necessary adjustments.
* Maintains healthy professional boundaries while demonstrating the flexibility and commitment required in frontline community-based work.
* Practices trauma-informed leadership, managing relationships, workload, and organizational change while maintaining personal well-being.
* Participates in supervision meetings, quality improvement activities, agency committees, peer reviews, and trainings.
* Demonstrates cultural responsiveness by working with the whole person in a welcoming, inclusive, respectful manner that embodies cultural humility.
* Seeks continuous professional development and uses performance evaluations and feedback for growth.

**Professional Ethics & Compliance**

* Maintains healthy interpersonal boundaries and adheres to all agency and industry ethical standards, including mandated reporting and participant confidentiality.
* Ensures compliance with all agency and program policies, including Boundary Code of Ethics, Core Competencies, Code of Conduct

jobs.description:
***Schedule: (Monday to Friday 8am-4:30pm)***

***Pay: $25.50-$38.50***

**ABOUT LIFEMOVES**

LifeMoves is the largest and most effective provider of housing and services for neighbors experiencing homelessness in Silicon Valley since 1987. Our Mission is to end homelessness by providing interim housing, supportive services, and building collaborative partnerships. With 40 programs, LifeMoves gives our neighbors experiencing homelessness a temporary place to call home while providing intensive, customized case management through site-based programs and community outreach.

**POSITION PURPOSE**

LifeMoves | First Step for Families (FSF) provides interim supportive housing in San Mateo to 39 families. During their stay, clients participate in holistic services tailored to each household’s unique needs and goals. Clients receive support to build self-sufficiency and return to housing stability, including but not limited to accommodations, meals, laundry, case management, and therapy. The team supports clients with housing, employment, benefits, physical and behavioral health through case management, workshops, and connection to specialized resources.

The First Step for Families Interim Supportive Housing (ISH) Case Manager (CM) reports to the site Program Director and provides case management, supports daily site operations, maintains a safe and welcoming environment, monitors the site, responds to client needs, and supports client check-ins, group activities, and overall site coordination. The position plays a key role in supporting people moving toward safe, stable housing and greater self-sufficiency. They provide case management services, life skills support, and resource connections and work in partnership with clients to set goals, celebrate progress, and overcome challenges. Using a trauma-informed and strengths-based approach, this position builds trust and respect, making sure clients feel heard, valued, and supported throughout their journey.

Key responsibilities include supporting clients by connecting them to services, building support networks, facilitating groups and activities, advocating for equitable access, and providing crisis intervention when needed. Beyond working directly with clients, this role may help to improve the overall program by sharing ideas, identifying service gaps, and helping strengthen community relationships. This role maintains clear documentation, contributes to program planning and reporting, and models professional, ethical behavior and works closely with their teammates to provide high-quality, coordinated care. Through their efforts, staff empower clients to grow their strengths, reach their goals, and build a better future.

**ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Client Support and Case Management**

* Develop and maintain individualized case plans focused on housing, employment, benefits, and overall well-being, based on each client’s strengths and goals.
* Support clients with housing searches, employment readiness, benefits enrollment (e.g., General Assistance, CalFresh, CAPI), and skill-building activities such as budgeting and daily living.
* Connect clients to healthcare providers and community resources, and assist with coordination, scheduling, and transportation as needed.
* Maintain accurate and timely client documentation and outcome tracking in HMIS and the agency’s client management system.
* Advocate for client needs and rights when working with partners, landlords, employers, or service agencies; provide mediation and conflict resolution support as needed.
* Provide calm, trauma-informed crisis response and ensure all client services align with ethical standards and agency values.

**Resource Connection and Community Collaboration**

* Build and maintain partnerships with community organizations, public agencies, and system partners (e.g., VA, APS, CPS, Probation) to support clients and improve access to resources.
* Serve as a liaison between LifeMoves and community stakeholders by sharing information, coordinating services, and promoting trauma-informed care practices.

**General Agency Responsibilities**

* Participate in weekly case conferences, monthly trainings, and regular supervision to strengthen skills.
* Fully participate in all required trainings. This includes completing trainings by assigned deadlines, actively engaging during sessions, and applying learnings to daily work.
* Attend continuing education opportunities to grow expertise and uphold agency standards.
* Be available to work occasional evenings and weekends as needed or as schedule describes.
* Perform other duties as assigned to meet program and organizational needs.

**Operations and Site Responsibilities**

* Support daily site operations, including inspections, maintenance coordination, donation management, and general facility upkeep.
* Assist with maintaining clean, safe, and organized living environments.
* Facilitate group sessions or workshops that promote skill development and confidence.

**SHIFT –** Monday-Friday 10:00am-6:30pm

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Educational Requirements:** Associate's Degree in related field preferred; or High School Diploma/GED with 2-5 years of equivalent experience in related field. Related fields may include direct involvement in peer advocacy, community outreach, housing services or roles within the homelessness services field.
* **Technology:** Comfortable using basic technology, including phone and messaging systems, email, Microsoft and Google Suites, and databases to complete administrative tasks and case management, reporting, and tracking outcomes.

Service Level Qualifications:

* **Care, Respect, Empathy:** Demonstrates empathy, professionalism, and respect for all individuals. **Emotional Regulation:** Stays calm and supportive in stressful situations and uses de-escalation skills. **Documentation:** Maintains clear documentation and organization. **Organization/Prioritization:** Organized, detail-oriented

jobs.description:
Business Operations Manager (7378U), Bakar Bio Labs #89972 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
UC Berkeley is the flagship campus of the University of California, internationally renowned for intellectual endeavors, particularly in life sciences and engineering. To equip UC Berkeley with one of the finest global centers of innovation and entrepreneurship, the Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley (BBLB) has been created as the flagship innovation center bringing together scholars, entrepreneurs, recent alumni, and industry - working at the interface of the life sciences and engineering - to translate their academic innovation out into the world as startups and as leaders. The mission of this unit is three-pronged: 1) Create essential & high visibility capabilities: rare, sought-after tough tech labs to attract industry and start-up innovators; 2) Chart a path for sustainable innovation for this generation and those to come: Establish a revenue-generating incubator that harnesses campus proximity and vibrant programs for students and researchers; and 3) Bolster our community and link to the greater world: Galvanize UC Berkeley's spokes of innovation and entrepreneurship, while providing a portal through which innovators from across UC, the State of California, and around the globe will join us.

MongoDB is seeking a technical, execution-obsessed individual to join the Recruiting Operations team as a RecOps Partner. In this role, you will oversee RecTech and Process Optimization, serving as the primary strategic partner and operational liaison to HR Tech, translating Talent Acquisition strategy into an actionable systems roadmap. You will architect complex operational workflows, drive complex, multi-quarter roadmaps and bring the technical fluency and business acumen needed to evaluate the viability and impact of technical solutions.

Reporting directly to the Sr. Manager, CoreOps, you will operate with high autonomy to drive cross-functional execution and change management. You will provide strategic guidance, technical domain oversight, and peer mentorship to other individuals within the team, supporting them as individual product owners of their deliverables while elevating operational rigor across the team.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in New York City, Austin, Palo Alto, or San Francisco for our hybrid working model.

### **What You'll Do**

* Drive RecTech Modernization & Tooling Strategy: Act as the primary liaison to HR Tech to distill TA vision into a cohesive technology roadmap. Oversee high-complexity initiatives, such as the deployment of our Offer-to-Hire workflow using AI and automation and pilots for enterprise-grade interview and debrief intelligence suites
* Architect Complex Workflows & Systems: Develop end-to-end process maps for all key recruiting workflows to identify friction points and structural opportunities. Architect major workflow redesigns, such as overhauling the end-to-end offer process to minimize manual interventions
* Optimize Greenhouse as a Core System of Work: Consolidate high-priority issue areas across the hiring lifecycle to eliminate fragmented, manual workflows. Leverage native Greenhouse features and strategic integrations to standardize processes, lower compliance risks, eliminate administrative overhead, and elevate data integrity
* Drive Cross-Functional Execution & Autonomy: Independently own and drive goals, steering change management and adoption across global teams for all systems and process updates. Resolve complex escalations, operating with autonomy while proactively flagging for support when necessary
* Mentor Junior Members of the Team: Act as a dedicated mentor and sounding board for the RecTech and Process Optimization sub-domain owners, supporting their development into strong Product Owners without having direct administrative or people management duties
* Leverage Data to Drive Strategic Outcomes: Proactively identify internal TA needs (recruiters, coordinators, hiring teams), act as a compelling communicator across cross-functional groups, and regularly leverage data diagnostics to drive operational outcomes

### **What You'll Bring**

* Advanced Expertise: 8+ years of experience architecting complex operational workflows, recruiting technology evaluations and implementations, and multi-quarter systems roadmaps
* Scope & Complexity: Proven track record of independently owning multi-faceted goals, driving cross-functional execution, and resolving complex operational escalations. Operates with high autonomy and demonstrates sound judgment on when to flag for escalation
* Commitment to Mentorship & Influence: Proactively identifies TA needs, acts as a compelling communicator across technical and non-technical stakeholders, and demonstrates a proven ability to mentor and uplevel junior team members
* Technical Aptitude & Tooling Expertise: Deep technical knowledge of core recruiting platforms (e.g., Greenhouse, Gem, Guide). Proven track record of evaluating tool ROI systematically, sunsetting redundant platforms, and experimenting with automations and AI in recruiting workflows
* Workflow Architecture & People Team Alignment: Demonstrated experience redesigning complex hiring workflows and partnering with downstream teams (HRIS, HR Operations, FP&A) to ensure cross-system alignment and data hygiene
* Hands-On Data Fluency: Comfortability extracting and diagnosing pipeline and operational data directly in Google Sheets using advanced formulas to run ad-hoc analyses and diagnose root causes

### **About MongoDB**

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB's unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we're powering the next era of software.

Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It's what makes us MongoDB.

To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we're committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employees' wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Underpinning this mission is a culture that aligns perfectly with what we want to achieve. We enable our people to grow, we support them in their learning and we reward them in so many different ways. Syner-G was recently honored with BioSpace's prestigious "Best Places to Work" 2027 award, for the fourth consecutive year, along with many other award-winning programs to make a career here truly life-enhancing. These recognitions are a testament to our commitment to fostering a positive and engaging work environment for our employees, with a particular emphasis on culture, career growth and development opportunities, financial rewards, leadership and innovation.

At Syner-G, we recognize that our team members are our most valuable asset. Join us in shaping the future, where your talents are valued, and your contributions make a meaningful impact.

For more information, visit www.Synergbiopharma.com

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**

Syner-G is seeking a Document Management Project Manager to support capital projects through effective document control, system administration, training, and user adoption activities. This role will serve as a subject matter resource for project documentation processes, document management systems, and Autodesk Forma, ensuring that project teams maintain accurate, compliant, and accessible project records throughout the project lifecycle.

The successful candidate will support capital project teams by managing documentation workflows, facilitating training sessions, leading onboarding activities, conducting Q&A support sessions, and driving adoption of document management best practices. This individual will collaborate with engineering, construction, facilities, and project stakeholders to ensure documentation standards are consistently applied across projects.

This position is internally classified as a Project Manager and will have a primary focus on project management.

**WORK LOCATION:**

Travel to client sites may be required based on project demands and training requirements.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

(This list is not exhaustive and may be supplemented or adjusted as necessary.)

* Serve as the primary resource for project document management processes and best practices.
* Manage and maintain capital project documentation throughout project planning, design, construction, commissioning, and closeout phases.
* Support document control activities, including document review workflows, version control, approval routing, retention, and archival processes.
* Administer and support Autodesk Forma and other project information management platforms.
* Develop, maintain, and improve document management procedures, standards, and work instructions.
* Facilitate onboarding sessions for new project team members and stakeholders utilizing document management systems.
* Deliver instructor-led and virtual training sessions related to document management processes, Autodesk Forma, and project documentation requirements.
* Conduct recurring Q&A sessions, office hours, and user support forums to address system and process questions.
* Provide first-level troubleshooting and user support for document management tools and workflows.
* Monitor document compliance and completeness throughout the project lifecycle.
* Coordinate with project managers, engineers, contractors, and external stakeholders to ensure required documentation is submitted, reviewed, and approved in accordance with project standards.
* Support data migration, document uploads, metadata management, and system organization activities.
* Generate document control reports, dashboards, and metrics to track adoption, compliance, and project documentation status.
* Assist with project turnover, ensuring complete and accurate documentation packages are delivered to operations and facilities teams.
* Maintain training materials, user guides, quick-reference documents, and standard operating procedures.
* Identify opportunities to improve document management workflows and enhance user experience.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements below represent the education, experience, skills, knowledge, and abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

*Education:*

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Information Management, Business, Education, or a related field preferred.
* Training, change management, or document control certifications are a plus.

*Technical Experience:*

* 3-7+ years of experience in document management, document control, project coordination, project support, or related roles.
* Experience supporting Capital Expenditure (CapEx) projects and associated documentation requirements.
* Experience administering or supporting Autodesk Forma strongly preferred.
* Experience working with document management systems, project collaboration platforms, or Common Data Env
